title: Cross-team dependency ledger with rolling commitments and OKR alignment
creator: Aisha Karim
description:
Problem: roadmap handoffs in the last two quarters show frequent last-minute blockers caused by ambiguous ownership, drifting timelines, and no canonical place tying commitments to OKRs. That creates churn for Launch weeks and reduces confidence for Dedicated/Private customers who require predictable windows.

Goal: build a lightweight Cross-team Dependency Ledger that: 1) records explicit per-cycle commitments (owner, acceptance criteria, slack/buffer), 2) surfaces OKR alignment for each commitment, 3) provides a rolling-commitment history (versioned ledger) so teams can see changes and reason about risk, and 4) integrates into the Console and Linear to enable automated reminders, escalation, and a single-pane readiness score.

Scope: MVP will include a ledger UI embedded in Console (read/write for PMs), a Linear sync (two-way for titles/status/owners), an OKR tagging layer (map commitment -> OKR(s)), and a simple readiness badge (green/amber/red) based on time-to-due, open dependencies, and owner confidence survey. Not included: policy automation for contractual SLAs (follow-on).

Success metrics: adoption by 4 product squads + infra + security in Cycle 2025-W11, reduction in last-minute cut requests by 40% for targeted initiatives, and >80% accurate lineage from ledger items -> Linear tickets within one week of creation.

Non-goals: replace the full dependency orchestration platform (this is a coordination ledger + visibility layer).

Implementation notes: ledger entries are immutable once committed (new versions created for each change) so we can audit who changed a commitment and why. We'll expose a small events API for other systems to consume (webhooks) and write a minimal webhook consumer in Console to render updates. Data model will be flattened key-value pairs to keep Linear sync predictable.

Open questions: what tolerance window should flip readiness from green->amber? (Product suggests 14 days; Eng suggests 7 days for infra-owned work). Need to finalize the acceptance schema and whether design should own UX of badges or Console infra team should.

Docs & artifacts: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ROADMAP-LEDGER-MVP (draft); Figma: https://figma.com/file/abcd1234/ledger-mvp; RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/121
comments: 2025-02-21 • Aisha Karim: Kickoff notes posted to Confluence; reached out to Infra and Security for intake meeting next week. Added initial success metrics. Action: Luca to draft sync contract between Linear <-> Ledger.

2025-02-25 • Luca Marin: Prototype wireframes in Figma and high-level API contract added. Asked Eng to estimate webhook cadence. ENG feedback: prefer event batching to avoid hot loops; will prototype 5m batch aggregation.

2025-02-28 • Priya Sethi (Engineering lead): Reviewed data model. Trade-off: immutable versions simplify audits but increase storage; propose compaction policy after 6 months. Blocking: need RBAC guardrails for edit paths — SEC input required.

2025-03-01 • Mateo Ruiz (Design): UX review—recommended per-cycle timeline view + a condensed mobile-friendly card. Suggested microcopy for readiness badges. Next: iterate on accessibility contrast for badge colors.

2025-03-03 • Jordan Lee (Security): Security review notes: require KMS-protected ledger backups for Private customers and audit log entries for all edits. We can scope backup as opt-in for MVP but audit logs must be present. Follow-up: SEC-907 created for audit retention policy.

2025-03-04 • Luca Marin: Implementation plan split into two workstreams: (1) Linear sync + webhook events (ENG-19832) and (2) Console UI + badge UX (DES-4412). Set weekly sync checkpoints; next demo scheduled 2025-03-18.
